tweets.body:
We're growing rapidly at @RadicalNumerics and scaling our core teams. Join us in building the next generation of scientific world models.

We're hiring across a few roles, each with significant ownership and cross-functional scope:

- Member of Technical Staff, Post-Training
- Member of Technical Staff, Infrastructure and Training Systems
- Member of Technical Staff, Pretraining Science  
- Member of Technical Staff, AI Bio
- Member of Technical Staff, Biosecurity

Our technology brings together numerics, systems engineering, and architecture design to tackle large-scale pretraining on scientific data. Our blogs (see below) give a flavor of the work.

We believe that advancing capabilities must go hand-in-hand with advancing safety and biosecurity. The same systems that design biology must also help defend against it.

Ping me or others in the team if you'd like to learn more.

https://t.co/LaC63aXZ5l

tweets.body:
What a great way to start the year, with a fun deep dive on 4-bit pretraining recipes.

If “mixed precision” still makes you think bfloat16, maybe with a dash of float8 compute, or float16 + loss scaling, check out our post for an overview of more modern methods.

Low-precision recipes are often treated as a given, but they’re an integral part of the co-development process across architecture, scaling, and training objectives, especially when new approaches shift activation and gradient distributions.

RND1 is important to me on a personal level: it symbolizes our commitment to open-source exploration of radically different designs for AI at scale — training objectives, architectures, domains. We are not done yet. More on Monday (the next one is for model architecture enthusiasts!).

tweets.body:
Life update: I started Radical Numerics with Stefano Massaroli, Armin Thomas, Eric Nguyen, and a fantastic team of engineers and researchers. We are building the engine for recursive self‑improvement (RSI): AI that designs and refines AI, accelerating discovery across science and industry.

Three core beliefs:
- We need orders of magnitude more AI systems in the world: models and interfaces built with purpose, to augment specific domains and workflows
- The complexity and resources required to develop AI are growing rapidly. Human development speed is the bottleneck.
- The process of developing frontier AI in new domains is ripe for disruption.

tweets.body:
It's easy (and fun!) to get nerdsniped by complex architecture designs. But over the years, I've seen hybrid gated convolutions always come out on top in the right head-to-head comparisons.

The team brings a new suite of StripedHyena-style decoder models, in the form of SLMs designed for edge devices. For these architectures, we opted for a short explicit (SE) convolution parametrization that brings speedups across a range of practical prompt lengths.

Amazing work from the pretraining, post-training, and infrastructure teams for bringing these models to life!

tweets.body: [6/7] Evo 2 has a 1-million-token context length. We trained for a substantial number of tokens at this scale, made possible by the architecture’s improved efficiency. We were pleased to see perplexity steadily decrease with both model scale and context length during our multi-stage mid-training procedure.

tweets.body: [5/7] All the gory pretraining details are available in Savanna. Savanna builds on DeepSpeed, GPT-NeoX, and TransformerEngine, optimizing for graceful scaling at the thousand GPU scale. tweets.title: [4/7] It is important for new architectures to target regimes of practical utility, rather than focusing solely on extremely long contexts where the asymptotics
tweets.body: [4/7] It is important for new architectures to target regimes of practical utility, rather than focusing solely on extremely long contexts where the asymptotics of attention dominate. Most pretraining costs are incurred by larger models operating on shorter sequences. We designed StripedHyena 2 and its operators to achieve speedups across the a range of practical sequence lengths

tweets.title: [3/7] Evo 2 required a significant investment in both research and engineering—from architecture design, derivation and implementation of new context-parallel a
tweets.body:
[3/7] Evo 2 required a significant investment in both research and engineering—from architecture design, derivation and implementation of new context-parallel algorithms, to large-scale training optimization.

Strong byte-level architectures such as StripedHyena 2 will unlock new applications for foundation models. I hope to see a return to ideas from signal processing and numerical methods in architecture design. There is still much to do, as many methods in these domains were optimized for an earlier era, different scales, and different hardware.

tweets.title: [2/7] I am excited about Evo 2 for many reasons. It is undoubtedly a leap forward in our ability to understand and generate genomes. I also hope it 2 can help p
tweets.body:
[2/7] I am excited about Evo 2 for many reasons. It is undoubtedly a leap forward in our ability to understand and generate genomes. I also hope it 2 can help push progress on real open-source in AI, continuing the work of so many @AiEleuther  @jeremyphoward  @allen_ai 
. Unfortunately, we have been seeing few truly open models in recent times, only open weights releases.

Interestingly, the largest Evo 2 model was trained on roughly the same order of magnitude of compute as DeepSeek V3, the language model that shook the field recently.
